messages:
cheng: ran a focused nsys + nccl trace on a 4xA100 TP job with dynamic batching + KV cache enabled. observed compute kernels and all-reduce never overlapping — big idle gaps on GPUs during the mid-token phase. nvtx shows kernel launches on stream 2 then a blocking NCCL allreduce on stream 0. attaching short timeline excerpt and command we used.

cheng: nsys cmd: `nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl --capture-range=cpu:begin,end --sample=none --duration=45 --force-overwrite -- ./run_inference.sh --tp 4 --batching dynamic`

cheng: timeline excerpt (simplified):
```
GPU0 | kernel_kv_prefetch __ -------------compute--------__ | idle | nccl_allreduce --------------------|
GPU1 | kernel_small_matmul __---compute---__ | idle | nccl_allreduce --------------------|
GPU2 | kernel_large_matmul __compute----__ | idle | nccl_allreduce --------------------|
GPU3 | kernel_selector_decide -> launch on stream2 -> cudaLaunchKernel | cudaStreamSynchronize(stream0) // NCCL
```

sam: can you paste the exact nvprof/nspy/nccl logs or a link? is this reproducible with kv cache off?

cheng: link: <redwood-perf:/runs/1768765439/nsys.zip> (timeline + nccl trace). reproduced 3/3 tries. when I flip REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=0 the all-reduce gaps shrink ~35% but compute kernels then get more memory pressure.

anya: quick thought: looks like kernel_selector is picking a small-block kernel early which is cheap, then when seq_len grows it switches to a large-block kernel that is synchronous on the default stream. if NCCL is using the default stream too we get stream-ordering stalls. we should ensure comms use a dedicated non-blocking stream or make selector prefer non-blocking variants when in TP mode. @cheng can you check which stream NCCL was using? :eyes:

perf-bot: perf-bot summary: anomaly detected: inter-GPU idle window spike at tokens 24-56. KV eviction rate +2.7x at same window. NCCL timelines show serialized launches on stream 0.

lucas: short repro patch idea: create a dedicated comm stream per worker and use cudaEvent records for ordering. small diff:
```
// old
ncclCommInitRank(&comm, nranks, id, rank);
comm_stream = cudaStreamDefault; // implicit
// new
cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(&comm_stream, cudaStreamNonBlocking);
ncclCommSetAsyncProgress(comm, 1); // if supported
// when launching kernels:
cudaEventRecord(ev, compute_stream);
cudaStreamWaitEvent(comm_stream, ev, 0);
```

lucas: also check kernel dispatcher: if kernel variant sets `needs_host_sync=true` we should force it onto a stream that won't block comms.

maria: quick experiments: 1) REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=0 reduced idle but cost token/sec. 2) set REDWOOD_KERNEL_HEURISTIC=latency_prefer reduced large-block selection and improved overlap by ~18% in my run. pushing a perf job now with both changes.

sam: this matches earlier bug where selector favored smaller l2-friendly kernels that serialized with NCCL. iirc we added a fallback path that sets `cudaStreamSynchronize` on corner cases. can we grep for `cudaStreamSynchronize(` in dispatcher?

cheng: grep shows two spots: one in kv_handshake (legacy) and one in kernel_selector fallback for 'non-cudaGraph' path. attaching snippet:
```
if (!cudaGraphCapturing()) {
  // fallback path
  cudaStreamSynchronize(stream);
}
```

anya: that `!cudaGraphCapturing()` fallback is ancient and forces ordering. propose: remove synchronize and rely on event-based waits + comm stream. will run a local branch removing it and run microprofile.

perf-bot: scheduled: perf-bot queued a 4xA100 nsys run with (kv_cache on/off) + (comm stream patch) for 6h. job id perf-1768765439-1.

sam: action items: @anya try branch removing the sync; @lucas prototype comm stream + events; @maria run perf matrix with REDWOOD_KERNEL_HEURISTIC=latency_prefer; @cheng collect nccl traces and compare token windows. please post short numbers in this thread.

cheng: thanks team — I'll upload the full nsys timeline and NCCL peer-to-peer logs once the runs finish and mark this thread with perf-id. starting with low-risk changes (comm stream + heuristic toggles) before we nuke kv cache. :thumbsup:
